narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimates you have a 53.4% chance of failing the bar exam on the first attempt. That means, based on the available information, failure is slightly more likely than success. This does not make failure certain, but it is a risk the law school was not willing to take.

The most important reason for this decision was your academic standing in your third year. You finished in the lowest decile of your class for that year, while students who were accepted typically sat around the sixth decile. This is a very strong signal pointing toward bar exam difficulty, and it carried the most weight in the decision. It tells the school that, despite your earlier performance, your trajectory at the end of your undergraduate studies was concerning.

On a more positive note, your undergraduate GPA worked in your favor. At 3.40, you are above the average of accepted students, which pulled the prediction toward passing. Similarly, being from an upper-middle income background—a group well represented among accepted students—also nudged the prediction slightly toward success. But these helpful factors could not overcome the negative impact of your third-year decile.

Please do not see this as a final judgment. You can strengthen your application by retaking key courses, improving your grades, and preparing thoroughly for the LSAT. If you demonstrate a stronger academic record over the next year, you will present a very different profile to law schools.
